title: To Kill a Mockingbird

vibeProfile.oneLine: A girl watches her father defend a Black man in the segregated South.

summary: In a small Alabama town during the Depression, young Scout Finch watches her lawyer father, Atticus, defend a Black man falsely accused of rape, while she and her brother slowly learn about courage, prejudice and the mysterious neighbour Boo Radley. Harper Lee's beloved novel filters a hard story about racial injustice through a child's clear eyes, and became one of the most read and taught books in America. Warm, moving and morally serious, it has shaped how generations think about fairness.
whyReadIt: A beloved, moving classic about justice seen through a child's eyes. Warm and hard-hitting at once.

funFacts.text: It won the Pulitzer Prize and was Lee's only published novel for over fifty years.
